operations.comment: ; ===== Championship Bowling (Another Ltd. / Romstar, 1989), NES CNROM =====
; Readable source maintained in the commentary phase; it rebuilds the ROM
; byte for byte with ca65/ld65 (binary pieces come from image.nes).
; Memory layout: one fixed 32 KiB PRG ROM at CPU $8000-$FFFF (file offsets
; 16-32783, no PRG banking) and four 8 KiB CHR ROM banks selected through
; SelectChrBank. Rough PRG map:
;   $8000-$CF84  game code (pins, ball, scoring, screens) with its tables
;   $CF85-$E00A  screen descriptors, palettes, attribute and nametable data
;   $E02B-$F19F  sound driver, its tables and the music/effect streams
;   $F1A0-$FF09  Reset/NMI and a general library (PPU queues, fades, math,
;                joypad, metasprites); several library routines are unreachable
;   $FFFA        vectors
; Main RAM use: $00-$6C library/zero-page work areas and game variables,
; $DF-$EA sound driver frame, $0200-$02D7 palette/attribute buffers,
; $0300-$03EF scores and pins, $03F0-$04AF timers, ObjTable and TileBuffer,
; $0500-$05A0 sound driver, $0600/$0700 sprite buffers.
; Region comments "; Code; Observed; physical a..b" mark the phase-1
; classification regions (physical file offsets) and their provenance.
; "Observed" code ran in recorded natural play; "Static" code is supported by
; static decoding only (unreachable library routines and code islands, plus a
; few small unreached branches; leads L-001/L-002/L-014).
; Dormant NMI jobs: the bodies of NmiUploadAttrRow, NmiVramRead, NmiFillRect,
; the column mode of NmiCopyStrip, the alternating sprite order in
; CopySpritesToDmaPage and the WaitSeconds countdown in the NMI are reachable
; but never run, because no reachable store (direct, indexed or indirect)
; opens their gate variable. They are still code. FillNametable2/3 are
; unreachable: nothing references them and FillNametable1's bne is always taken.
; The remaining small Static branches in reachable routines are explained where
; they occur: the stepped fade paths (FadeDelay is $FF only inside
; AnnounceBowler), two sound-driver clamps and the envelope restart that ROM
; sound data never needs, DrawObject's unused $FD list jump, three page carries
; that the address arithmetic rules out, and PlaceSprite's out-of-range Y path,
; which no object's position and frame offsets can reach.
; Unreachable code (L-001/L-002): 23 runs, 1461 bytes, lie outside the control
; flow closure from the Reset/IRQ and NMI vectors. A census of every computed
; transfer (jmp (ind), the sound driver's RTS dispatch, stack writes, RTI)
; found none that can reach them, so they are dead in this build. They are
; still code: inline-argument conventions and immediates sized to the data
; they use. Each is marked "unreachable" where it is defined.
; ===== Symbols: hardware registers, RAM variables and constants =====
; sound frame (X = $DF) fields: logical channel 0-7 / output stage: APU channel
; general scratch byte (also FadeGroupMask / PadValue in the library)
; CopyRectToPpu parameters ($01-$06)
; channel * 2 (index into word arrays)
; scratch; TitleScreen returns players - 1 here
; 16-bit stream read pointer (lo, hi); hi = 0 means channel idle
; scratch / loop counter; TitleMenu keeps lane - 1 here
; scratch
; channel bit mask (bit n = logical channel n)
; scratch
; output stage: music channel bit (1,2,4,8)
; ApplyHookAndAdvance: pointer to the selected curve
; AnimateDeckPin: pointer to the selected fall animation
; scratch pointer (also the parameter of the sprite group setters)
; output stage: effect channel bit ($10..$80) that overrides it
; output stage: pointer to the APU registers $4000+4n
; driver scratch
; pointer to a screen descriptor (LaneScreenDesc, TitleScreenDesc, ...)
; driver scratch
; Multiply16x16 product bytes 2-3
; pointer to a decimal-digit buffer
; controller 1, bit7..0 = A B Select Start Up Down Left Right
; controller 2, same layout
; value NMI writes to PPUCTRL after its VRAM work
; offset of the current object descriptor in ObjTable (0, 10, 20, ...)
; DrawObject: pointer to the current 4-byte sprite record
; DrawObject: hardware sprites still available to this object
; DrawObject: current OamBuffer offset
; DrawObject: 16-bit screen coordinate being built
; NMI queue: copy a rectangle from (BlockCopySrc) to the nametable
; NMI queue: fill a nametable rectangle with FillTile

; DrawRectListInline record list pointer
; NMI queue: 0 idle, 1 copy row (+1), other = copy column (+32, never queued)
; NMI queue: read VRAM into RAM (counts down; 1 = +1 increment)
; Upload1bppTiles parameters
; bit0/bit1: copy the 1bpp source into plane 0 / plane 1
; Upload1bppTilesInline return pointer
; NMI queue: upload one 8-byte attribute row
; offset of that row in AttrBuffer
; NMI queue: high byte of the attribute table ($23/$27/$2b), 0 = idle
; AttrBuffer offset for that upload ($00 or $40)
; NMI queue: 1 = background half, $11 = sprite half (value = index+1)
; source pointer for SetBgPaletteAndWait / SetSpritePaletteAndWait
; 0 normal, 1 request off, 2 off (main owns the PPU), 3 request on

; WaitSeconds countdown
; frames left in the current second (60)
; incremented around the CHR bank write

; Random rewrites its caller's saved A here
; 32 bytes: palette RAM image uploaded by the NMI
; 32 bytes: full-brightness palette that fades work toward
; $0240-$027f nametable 0 attributes, $0280-$02bf nametable 1
; frames per fade step, $ff = no fade (instant)
; 16-byte 2bpp tile assembled by Build2bppTile
; last read, used to reject DMC-corrupted reads
; [4][11] per frame: high nibble = first ball, low nibble = second ball (see ScoreBall)
; [4][11 words] running total after each frame
; 0 = frames 1-6, 1 = frames 7-10 on the scorecard overlay
; pins knocked over by the current ball (ball and pin-on-pin hits)
; total pins down in the current frame (10 = all)
; pins hit directly by the ball during this throw
; set when a pin of the back two rows (index >= 6) is moving
; [10, stride 5] lane-view pins: 0 standing, 1-5 sliding direction, $FE lying, $FF gone
; 1-9 rotation frame while sliding
; [10, stride 5] close-up pins: 0 standing, $1x-$Cx fall animation (high nibble = animation, low = step), $FE lying, $FF gone
; FrameTimers[0] reload: frames per ball movement step
; FrameTimers[1] reload: frames per lane-pin step
; FrameTimers[2] reload: frames per deck-pin animation step
; three countdowns decremented by the NMI (see TickFrameTimers)
; ObjTable: 10-byte object descriptors, X = ObjSlot; first hardware sprite
; ObjTable +1/+2: 16-bit screen X
; ObjTable +3/+4: 16-bit screen Y
; ObjTable +5: frame number (index into the frame pointer table)
; ObjTable +6/+7: pointer to the frame pointer table
; ObjTable +8: bit7 flip V, bit6 flip H, bit5 behind background
; ObjTable +9: hardware sprites reserved for the object
; ObjTable slot $0A: shared descriptor used to draw each lane-view pin
; ObjTable slot $14: ball in the close-up (perspective) view
; ObjTable slot $1E: the bowler while throwing, the pinsetter between balls, the sign girl
; RAM tile/text buffer used as BlockCopy/Strip source (up to 144 bytes, $041b-$04aa)
; nonzero once a button was pressed during the title animation
; four escape codes of the current compressed nametable
; 4 pending sound ids, $FF = empty; $0503 is played first
; nonzero while PlaySound edits the queue (driver skips the frame)
; X value of the driver's zero-page frame ($DF); also saves X in PlaySound
; channels that must (re)write all four APU registers this frame
; channels whose envelope produced a new value this frame
; channels with a running stream
; hardware outputs written this frame (bit of the owning channel)
; SndOwnedMask of the previous frame
; staged APU register values for one hardware channel
; [8] current note: octave*16 + semitone; $7C rest, $7F = no retrigger
; [8] subtracted from envelope volume
; [8] bits 7-6 square duty, bit 5 = load SndSweep once
; [8] note length in frames
; [8] index into EnvelopeTable
; [8] frames left in the current note
; [8] frames left in the current envelope step
; [8 words] saved stream pointers
; [8 words] return address for stream command $F0 (call)
; [8 words] envelope read pointers
; written once by SoundInit ($C0), never read
; 16-bit generator state (low, high); zeroed only by Reset
; sprite shadow built by the game (64 x Y, tile, attr, X)
; OamBuffer sprite 22 = lane-view ball. Y (counts down toward the pins)
; sprite 22 tile: nonzero while the ball rolls (also its animation frame)
; sprite 22 X (byte $065a is its attribute byte)
; OamBuffer sprite 23 = spin-meter marker. Y (from SpinMeterArc)
; sprite 23 tile ($70, set by RunSpinMeter)
; sprite 23 attributes (0)
; sprite 23 X (from SpinMeterArc)
; copy actually sent by OAM DMA ($4014 = $07)
; PPU control: NMI enable, sprite/background pattern tables, VRAM increment
; PPU mask: rendering enables
; PPU status: bit 7 = vblank flag (read clears it)
; sprite DMA from page $xx00
; controller 1 data / strobe for both ports
; controller 2 data / APU frame counter on write
; Sound ids (index into SoundHeaderTable); names describe where the game plays them
; ObjTable slot offsets (10-byte descriptors). Slot 0: close-up pins / title and celebration
; figures / selection cursor; slot 1: LanePinObj and second figures; slot 2: CloseBallObj;
; slot 3: ActorObj (bowler, pinsetter, sign girl).
; Scorecard mark tiles (CHR banks 1/2, pattern half $1000; checked in CHR)
; "-" ball that hit no pins
; "G" first ball with no pins, frames 1-9
; spare box
; strike box
; ===== End symbols =====
; iNES header: "NES", 2 x 16 KiB PRG, 4 x 8 KiB CHR, mapper 3, vertical mirroring.
; Developer signature: half-width katakana "bowling game" and
; "  1989 Another Ltd.  ". Not referenced by code.
; ===== Game flow =====
; GameStart - entered from Reset. Enables NMI (PpuCtrlShadow $90: NMI on,
; sprites from pattern table $1000), sets the fade speed, presets the
; high-score table (three totals of 200, empty names), then loops forever:
; title screen -> player selection -> game -> results -> title screen.
; 6 frames per fade step
; pausing allowed, but CheckPause is unreachable, so the game has no pause
; HighScores = 200, 200, 200; HighScoreNames cleared. Round-1 disassembly saw
; no display change after patching $C2-$C7; DrawTopHighScore only draws entry 0
; when the lane screen is built, which may explain that observation.
; TitleLoop - run the title/menu screen (it never returns X = $FF in practice);
; it leaves players - 1 in Temp1 and lane - 1 in Temp2.
; FrameLoop - one frame for the current bowler: reset the per-frame counters,
; draw the lane, (in multi-player games) announce the bowler, set up both pin
; views and the bowler.
; single player: no announcement
; BallLoop - one ball: aim (Left/Right, A to throw, B shows the scorecard),
; set power/control, animate the approach and release the ball.
; RollLoop - advance ball, lane-view pins and close-up pins each pass until
; the ball has stopped and every pin in both views has settled.
; carry clear while a lane pin still slides
; carry clear while a close-up pin still falls
; score the ball
; Frame finished when all ten pins are down or the 10th frame is complete
; (TenthFrameBall = 3); otherwise the second ball follows once.
; Second ball: remove the fallen pins and reset ball and bowler.
; EndOfFrame - clear the lane; advance this bowler's frame number (frames
; 1-9) or finish the 10th frame, then move to the next bowler.
; NextPlayer - rotate CurrentPlayer through 0..NumPlayersMinus1. Bowlers 1 and
; 3 (players 2 and 4) use controller 2, bowlers 0 and 2 controller 1
; (confirmed in a natural 4-player game).
; GameOver - when the next bowler has completed ten frames (FramesScored >= 10):
; play sound 8 (an empty header), show the final scorecard and the results.
; ShowLaneScreen - draw the lane screen, coloring palette entry $0222 with the
; lane's LaneColorTable value, then fade it in slowly (FadeDelay $0F = 15
; frames per step instead of the usual 6). The old delay is restored after.
; One background color per lane number (lanes 1-5).
; StartDeckPinFallByBall / StartDeckPinFallByPin - X = pin offset (0, 5, ...,
; 45). Choose the close-up fall animation from the lane-view sliding
; direction: DeckPinState = table[X + direction - 1]. Each table holds five
; entries per pin (directions 1-5), $10-$C0 = animation number * 16.
; BallHitFallAnims - fall animation code per (pin, direction) when the ball
; hits a pin: 10 pins x 5 directions (StartDeckPinFallByBall).
; PinHitFallAnims - the same layout for a pin knocked by another pin
; (StartDeckPinFallByPin).
; AnimateDeckPin - X = pin offset. Advance a falling close-up pin one step:
; the state's high nibble selects a 7-step animation in DeckPinAnimTable and
; the low nibble counts the step. Each step is 3 bytes (frame, dx, dy).
; After step 7, or when the pin leaves the X range $60-$9F, the pin is
; removed (state $FF, hidden).
; DeckPinAnimTable - 12 pointers (animations $1x-$Cx; indexed as
; (state >> 4) * 2 - 2) followed by twelve 21-byte animations of 7 steps
; (frame, dx, dy).
; RemoveAllDeckPins - hide every close-up pin that is not already removed
; (between the two balls of a frame).
; UpdateDeckPins - run AnimateDeckPin for every falling close-up pin when
; FrameTimers[2] expires (reloaded from DeckPinTimerReload). While the ball
; is touching pins, standing pins 7 and 8 (offsets $23, $28) are switched to
; frame $0A, apparently to restore their normal look; then all pins are drawn.
; KnockDeckPinSideways - unreachable from the vectors (L-001). X = pin offset; moves the
; pin to the left or right edge position from DeckPinSideX, sets frame 2
; and state $FE (lying).
; DeckPinSideX - left/right X pairs per pin for KnockDeckPinSideways.
; DrawDeckPins - copy each close-up pin into ObjTable slot 0 and draw it.
; CheckDeckPinsSettled - carry clear if some close-up pin is still falling
; (state other than 0, $FE, $FF).
; SetupDeckPins - place the ten close-up pins standing, using
; DeckPinStartXY (Y raised by $1B) and hardware sprites $22, $24, ...
; DeckPinStartXY - ten (X, Y) pairs: head pin, then rows of 2, 3 and 4 pins.
; DeckPinObjTemplate - descriptor template for the close-up deck pins
; (2 sprites each, frame table DeckPinFrames).
; first hardware sprite
; X, Y

; flags, sprite budget
; DeckPinFrames - 21 frame pointers into the close-up pin sprite records.
; Close-up pin sprite records (DrawObject format). Frames are stored in a
; different order from the table; DeckPinFrame00 is the usual $FE hidden frame.
; UpdateCloseBall - while the lane-view ball is below Y $C4, project its

; ProjectCloseBall - computes the close-up position once the ball is past

; UpdateLanePins - for each lane-view pin: a standing pin hit by the ball
; starts sliding (direction from ChoosePinDirection, sound $2D, both hit

; ChoosePinDirection - from ball (CollideAX/AY) and pin (CollideBX/BY):

; UpdateLaneBall - every FrameTimers[0] expiry move the rolling ball: apply the

; Two lane-view roll frames that alternate while the ball moves.
; ApplyHookAndAdvance - once the ball is past HookStartY, add the next value of
; the selected 16-step curve (signed X offsets) to LaneBallX; the curve then
; repeats its last entry. The ball always advances 2 pixels in Y.
; HookCurvePtrs - one pointer per HookCurveIndex value (0-8, chosen on the

; HookCurves - nine 16-byte curves of signed per-step X offsets, applied once

; The set is mirror-symmetric around curve 4: curves 0-3 move left ($FF-$FD),
; curve 4 is straight, curves 5-8 move right (1-3), and the outer curves
; break earlier and harder.
; ResetLaneBall - copy LaneBallStart (Y $D0, frame $0E, X $D4) and restart the hook.
; Lane-view ball start values for LaneBallY, LaneBallFrame, (unused byte), LaneBallX.
; AnimateApproach - seven 16-frame steps of the bowler's run-up: frames
; advance (until frame 10) with a footstep sound and the bowler moves up 4
; pixels per step.
; AimAndWaitForThrow - first ball of frame 1 starts with the greeting
; animation. Then poll the active controller: Left/Right move the bowler
; (and the lane-view ball between X $C4 and $E4), B shows the scorecard,
; A (new press) plays sound $23, steps the bowler forward and returns.
; A pressed?
; only a new press counts

; Left or Right?

; DrawBowler - draw ObjTable slot $1E.
; BowlerGreeting - alternate bowler frames 1 and 2 three times (15 frames

; $0C: second ball knocked nothing

; 10th frame: which ball?
; first-ball strike in the 10th

; after a first-ball strike the frame continues
; open 10th frame: no third ball (+1 here, +1 below)
; second strike in the 10th
; third ball only after a strike or spare
; Open 10th frame: no third ball. Never taken in play, because an open 10th
; already sets TenthFrameBall to 3 after the second ball; defensive only.
; third ball goes into byte 10's high nibble
; TenthFrameBall++

; Build2bppTile - assemble one tile in TileBuildBuffer from (FontSrc) and
; advance FontSrc by 8.
; NmiFillRect - NMI job: fill FillRows rows of FillWidth tiles at FillPpuAddr
; with FillTile. Dormant in this build: no reachable store, direct or indexed,
; sets FillPending (only the job clears it).
; NmiBlockCopy / CopyBlockToPpu - NMI job: copy BlockCopyRows rows of
; BlockCopyWidth bytes from (BlockCopySrc) to BlockCopyPpuAddr (+32 per row).
; NmiCopyStrip - NMI job: copy StripLength bytes from (StripSrc) to
; StripPpuAddr, as a row (StripMode 1) or a column (other values, PPU +32
; increment). StripSrc advances so consecutive jobs continue the data.
; Every reachable store writes StripMode = 1, so the column path is dormant.
; UploadTilesInline - inline-argument routine (unreachable, L-001):
;   jsr UploadTilesInline
;   .word ppuAddress, source
;   .byte count               ; number of 16-byte tiles
; UploadTiles - same with the parameters in VramDest (PPU address), VramSrc
; and TileCount. Unreachable (L-001).
; BuildDateText2 - a second copy of the build string. Unreferenced.
; Unused $FF fill.
; CopyrightText - "1989.Another Ltd". Unreferenced.
; Unused $00 fill before the vectors.
; 6502 vectors: NMI = NMI ($F260), RESET = IRQ = Reset ($F22A).
; CHR ROM: four 8 KiB pattern banks (PPU only; bank n is selected together
; with palette set n by LoadPaletteSetAndChr: 0 title, 1 lane, 2 celebration /
; announcement, 3 results). Kept as binary; tile contents are not described here.
